author: Amanda Rhoades
title: 'The timing is wild': New Seasons cuts nearly 100 staff members following new labor agreement - NewsBreak
text:
By Amanda Rhoades Ariel Iacobazzi ,
1 days ago
PORTLAND, Ore. ( KOIN ) — Dozens of New Seasons employees were sent home from work today or received phone calls notifying them their jobs had been eliminated.
A New Seasons Market spokesperson confirmed to KOIN 6 News that 95 staff members had been cut across 20 different locations.
“We know layoffs are difficult and have real impacts on people and families,” the spokesperson said. “Following the ratification of a new labor agreement and wage increases across all stores, our ongoing labor costs have significantly increased.”
Feast on Lunar New Year food specials at these Portland restaurants The spokesperson said those increasing costs forced the company to reduce its staff, though the number of positions cut represents less than 5% of the current staff.
“These decisions were not made lightly, but they are necessary to protect the majority of our workforce and allow New Seasons Market to continue serving our communities,” the company spokesperson said. “We are working directly with affected employees and providing transition support that includes 4 weeks of pay and 6 weeks of continued health coverage.”

KOIN Morning Digest Produce clerk Joe Meyers got the news on Tuesday that many of his colleagues – who have become friends during his nearly 18 years with New Seasons Market – were laid off.
“It’s people’s job security, people’s livelihoods and how they put food on the table,” he told KOIN 6 News. “And they just, without consulting anyone, they just sort of decided today that they didn’t care about that.”
After multiple strikes throughout the last two years, unionized New Seasons workers approved a collective bargaining agreement with the company in December, which increased wages in an effort to keep pace with the rising cost of living.
With the agreement, the median wage of union employees increased to $23.37 per hour, and the minimum rate for new hires rose to $19 per hour. But this celebration was short-lived.
“The timing is wild,” said employee Erin Solar. “I feel caught off guard and very disappointed in New Seasons.”
Solar, who is a part of the New Seasons Labor Union (NSLU), added they are working with the people who lost their jobs.
While both she and Meyers still have their jobs, their hearts break for those who don’t.
“I’m just making sure that people know that it’s okay to be angry and we don’t have to just lay down and take it,” Meyers said. “There’s power in just being a worker and we’re all workers.”
Those 95 laid off employees will get paid for the next four weeks, although they won’t be working.
In the meantime, the NSLU says they are actively fighting the layoffs.
